verses.text: On the plains of Moab, beside the Jordan across from Jericho, the LORD said to Moses,
"Command the people of Israel to give the Levites towns to live in from the land they will own. Also give the Levites the pasture land around these towns.
The towns will be their homes, and the pasture land will be for their cattle, their flocks, and all their other animals.
The pasture land around each town you give the Levites must reach out about four hundred fifty metres from the town wall in every direction.

Outside the town, measure about nine hundred metres on the east side, nine hundred on the south side, nine hundred on the west side, and nine hundred on the north side, with the town in the middle. This will be their pasture land.
Six of the towns you give the Levites will be towns of safety, where a person who has killed someone may run for protection. Besides these, give them forty-two other towns.
In all, give the Levites forty-eight towns, together with their pasture land.

The towns you give the Levites will come from the land of the people of Israel. Take more towns from the larger tribes and fewer from the smaller tribes. Each tribe must give some of its towns to the Levites, according to the size of its land."
The LORD said to Moses,
"Speak to the people of Israel and tell them: When you cross the Jordan into the land of Canaan,
choose some towns to be your towns of safety. A person who kills someone by accident may run there for protection.
These towns will be a safe place from the relative who wants to pay back the killing, so that the person accused of killing will not die before he stands trial before the community.
The six towns you give will be your towns of safety.
Give three towns on the east side of the Jordan and three in the land of Canaan. They will be towns of safety.
These six towns will be places of safety for the people of Israel and for foreigners and visitors living among them. Anyone who kills someone by accident may run there.
But if someone strikes another person with an iron object and that person dies, he is a murderer. The murderer must be put to death.
If someone has a stone in his hand that could kill, and he strikes another person and that person dies, he is a murderer. The murderer must be put to death.
If someone has a wooden object in his hand that could kill, and he strikes another person and that person dies, he is a murderer. The murderer must be put to death.
The relative who pays back the killing must put the murderer to death himself. When he finds him, he must put him to death.
If someone pushes another person because he hates him, or throws something at him on purpose from a hiding place, so that he dies,

or if he hits him with his fist out of hatred, so that he dies, the one who struck him must be put to death. He is a murderer. The relative who pays back the killing must put the murderer to death when he finds him.
But someone may suddenly push another person without hating him, or throw something at him without planning it,
or, without seeing him, drop a stone on him that is big enough to kill, so that he dies. He was not his enemy and did not mean to harm him.
Then the community must judge between the one who killed and the relative who wants to pay back the killing, following these rules.

The community must protect the one accused of killing from the relative who wants revenge, and send him back to the town of safety where he ran. He must stay there until the death of the high priest who was anointed with the holy oil.
But if the one accused of killing ever goes outside the borders of the town of safety where he ran,
and the relative finds him outside the town and kills him, the relative will not be guilty of murder.
The one accused should have stayed in his town of safety until the high priest died. Only after the high priest's death may he go back to his own land.
These are rules and laws for you and for all your families to come, wherever you live.
Anyone who kills a person must be put to death as a murderer only on the word of witnesses. No one may be put to death on the word of just one witness.
Do not accept payment to spare the life of a murderer who deserves to die. He must be put to death.
And do not accept payment to let someone who ran to a town of safety go back and live on his own land before the high priest dies.

Do not make the land where you live unclean. Killing makes the land unclean, and nothing can make the land right with God after a person has been killed, except the death of the one who did the killing.
Do not make the land where you live unclean, the land where I live, for I, the LORD, live among the people of Israel."
